items.q: What are Treasure's seven deadly sins of speaking?
items.a: **Gossip, judging, negativity, complaining, excuses, embroidery, dogmatism.** Gossipers will do you next. Judging makes the listener feel scored. His mother on October 1: *"isn't it dreadful?"* Complaining is **viral misery**. Excuses are a **blamethrower**. Exaggeration cheapens language into lying. Dogmatism sells opinions as facts — you are **listening into the wind**.

items.q: Why is complaining worse than a bad mood?
items.a: It **spreads**. UK national sport (weather, sport, politics). It does not spread sunshine. The listener inherits the misery, so they stop listening.

items.q: What does HAIL stand for, and what else does the word mean?
items.a: **Honesty, Authenticity, Integrity, Love.** Also the verb: *greet or acclaim enthusiastically* — how words land if those four hold. Authenticity = **standing in your own truth**. Integrity = **be your word**.

items.q: Why put love next to honesty?
items.a: Absolute honesty can be cruelty: *"you look ugly this morning."* Love **tempers** it. And if you are really wishing someone well, it is **very hard to judge them at the same time**.

sections.title: Open the toolbox and warm it

items.q: Which vocal tools does Treasure pull out?
items.a: **Register** (chest = weight; we vote for lower voices) · **timbre** (hot-chocolate voice is trainable) · **prosody** (monotone and uptalk both fail) · **pace + silence** (do not fill with um) · **pitch** (same words, different meaning) · **volume** (loud or quiet; do not sodcast).

items.q: What warmup if you can only do one drill?
items.a: The **siren**: *we* (high) → *aw* (low). Full set before a raise, proposal, wedding, or stage: arms-up sigh, ba-ba-ba, kid lip trill, exaggerated la, rolled R, then siren. **No engine works well cold.**
